title: Diagnosing a Slow API with Application Insights
description: Use distributed tracing to find which downstream dependency is making your API slow.

data.text: Customers report that the checkout page takes 8 seconds to load. The page calls three services: an orders API, an inventory API, and a payment API. Your logs show nothing unusual — every service logs "request completed" with no errors. How do you find where the time goes?

Use **Application Insights** distributed tracing. Every service emits a **correlation id** (`operation_Id`) that is propagated on the `traceparent` header, so the whole fulfilment of one user request becomes a single timeline in the **Transaction Search** and **Application Map**. Because no errors are logged, you cannot use logs alone — you need the timing of each span.

data.title: Instrument a .NET API with Application Insights

data.text: Then run a Kusto query in **Logs** to rank the slowest spans for the checkout operation:

data.title: Kusto query — slowest dependencies per request
data.code:
let slowCheckout = requests
    | where name == "GET /checkout" and timestamp > ago(24h)
    | project operation_Id, requestDuration = duration, timestamp;
slowCheckout
| join kind=inner (dependencies
    | project operation_Id, span = name, target, spanDuration = duration)
    on operation_Id
| summarize avgSpan = avg(spanDuration), p95Span = percentile(spanDuration, 95)
          by span, target
| order by p95Span desc

data.text: Plain application logs cannot tell you **where** time was spent across process boundaries. Application Insights records each HTTP call, SQL query, and cache hit as a **dependency telemetry** event tagged with the same `operation_Id`, so you can attribute the 8 seconds without guessing.

cards.title: Raw application logs
cons: Cannot attribute time to a dependency
